added_models.model: Kissei chronically instrumented pregnant-sheep intravenous infusion model of KUR-1246 (bedoradrine) tocolysis reading maternal and fetal heart rate, blood pressure, electrolytes, lactate, glucose and insulin

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level (paywalled); Obstet Gynecol 100:487-494, print September 2002, no separate epub. Quote as rendered on PubMed/Europe PMC ('microg', 'K(+)'); the print text uses the micro sign and a superscript plus. Eight ewes at 123-125 days, oxytocin-driven contractions, KUR-1246 stepped 0.001 to 0.3 ug/kg/min over 3 h vs saline. The 24-h infusion at 0.03 ug/kg/min (Murata 2005 BJOG, https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1471-0528.2004.00333.x, PMID 15663400, the paper the checker calls Kanayama 2005) moved maternal heart rate, lactate, glucose and insulin but not electrolytes significantly and called the changes 'within the compensatory capacity'.
safety.judgement: Opening entry. A different system from the Kissei conscious-dog telemetry (Furihata 2006) and the rat organ bath: chronically instrumented pregnant ewes under stepwise intravenous infusion with electrolytes, lactate, glucose and insulin read, the one bedoradrine model that stated the metabolic harms. Safety only: its PD readout is uterine contraction, not an airway, and it set no airway exposure or margin.
safety.model: Kissei chronically instrumented pregnant-sheep intravenous infusion model of KUR-1246 (bedoradrine) tocolysis reading maternal and fetal heart rate, blood pressure, electrolytes, lactate, glucose and insulin
safety.note: Pregnant ewes infused stepwise to 0.3 ug/kg/min: above 0.03 heart rate, blood pressure, blood K+, lactate, glucose and insulin shifted; fewer such effects than ritodrine.
safety.short: Sheep predicted hypokalaemia, tachycardia at tocolytic doses
safety.quote: Significant differences between the two groups were found at high doses over 0.03 microg/kg/minute for the following parameters: maternal heart rate, diastolic blood pressure, mean blood pressure, base excess, blood K(+), blood lactate, plasma glucose, plasma insulin

safety.magnitude_basis: hypokalaemia and heart rate: sheep blood K+ and heart rate shifted above 0.03 ug/kg/min IV at tocolytic exposure; asthmatics at 3-60 ug/min IV had hypokalaemia as the second commonest AE (moderate in 2 of 40) and a mild dose-related heart-rate rise; species, doses and infusion regimens not comparable
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level (paywalled). n=40 stable asthmatics (MN-221-CL-004 dose escalation 3-60 ug/min; CL-005 fixed dose over 1 or 2 h, NCT00679263, results posted 2011-12-15). The registry AE table lists 'Hyperkalemia' 2/11 and 4/11 on MN-221 vs 1/6 placebo, the opposite direction to the paper's hypokalaemia that needed oral KCl, so the registry posting does not carry the comparison and the entry is dated to the paper (online 2012-10-25). House 2015 (n=167, 1200 ug in exacerbations) reports cardiovascular and metabolic effects consistent with beta2 agonism, no status change. Sheep blood lactate and glucose shifts have no bedoradrine patient record (Liedtke 2019 lists no bedoradrine).
safety.reason: Sheep hypokalaemia and tachycardia held in patients
safety.judgement: The sheep stated the harms (blood K+, heart rate, glucose, lactate) above the tocolytic dose, and hypokalaemia and a heart-rate rise both appeared in asthmatics at bronchodilating infusion rates: a direction match, made prospectively (2002, before any asthma trial), so same not retro. Counted here and not in dose because the sheep set no airway exposure or margin (decision 16). The model ran in another indication but the patient side is asthma, so nothing is imported.
safety.model: Kissei chronically instrumented pregnant-sheep intravenous infusion model of KUR-1246 (bedoradrine) tocolysis reading maternal and fetal heart rate, blood pressure, electrolytes, lactate, glucose and insulin
safety.note: Held: in 40 asthmatics hypokalaemia was the second commonest AE, moderate in two subjects and reversed with oral KCl, with a mild dose-related heart-rate rise.
safety.short: Hypokalaemia and tachycardia held in asthma patients
safety.quote: The most frequently reported AEs were tremor, hypokalemia, and headache.

added_models.model: Antwerp patient-specific computational fluid dynamics of HRCT airway geometries reading regional airway resistance 4 h after a single inhaled dose of carmoterol in asthmatics

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level (paywalled); J Biomech 41:106-113, online 2007-08-14, print January 2008. The abstract names only 'a novel long acting beta2 agonist (LABA) that acts shortly after inhalation'; carmoterol is identified from the record's indexed substances (MeSH: carmoterol). 14 mild-to-moderately severe asthmatics: 10 scanned before and 4 h after the dose, 4 scanned twice after bronchodilator wash-out as controls. No registry record found for this 2007 imaging study.
engagement.judgement: Opening entry at first public use. Not an animal: an in-silico airflow model solved on each patient's own CT geometry, so model_kind in_silico, its own track. The comparison with spirometry is in the same paper and follows as the next entry.
engagement.model: Antwerp patient-specific computational fluid dynamics of HRCT airway geometries reading regional airway resistance 4 h after a single inhaled dose of carmoterol in asthmatics
engagement.note: Patient-specific CFD on HRCT airway geometries, built to read regional airway resistance change after a single inhaled dose of carmoterol in 14 asthmatics.
engagement.short: Patient-CT CFD model built around carmoterol
engagement.quote: The aim of the present study was to improve the actual imaging techniques by subsequent analysis of the imaging data using computational fluid dynamics (CFD).

engagement.magnitude_basis: CFD total and distal airway resistance change vs FEV1 change 4 h after carmoterol in 10 asthmatics: r = -0.73 and -0.76, distal airway volume r = 0.69; a correlation, no fold error to compute
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level (paywalled). Active group FEV1 +8.78 +/- 6.27 % predicted vs -3.38 +/- 6.87 in controls. The source states the agreement itself (comparison_stated). Drug identity rests on the indexed substance list, not the abstract text; no registry record found.
engagement.reason: CFD resistance tracked FEV1 after carmoterol
engagement.judgement: Same on engagement: the model's own readout, regional airway resistance computed from the patient's CT, moved in dosed asthmatics and the paper states its agreement with spirometry. It is a concurrent readout validation in one experiment, not a prediction made before the patient result, so no retrodiction flag; it does not pick patients, so class level. A re-scorer who wants a model to precede its patient result may set this aside.
engagement.model: Antwerp patient-specific computational fluid dynamics of HRCT airway geometries reading regional airway resistance 4 h after a single inhaled dose of carmoterol in asthmatics
engagement.note: In 10 asthmatics FEV1 rose 8.8% predicted 4 h after carmoterol and CFD-computed total and distal airway resistance fell in step (r = -0.73, -0.76).
engagement.short: CFD airway resistance fell with FEV1
engagement.quote: All changes in the CFD-based calculated R(aw) significantly correlate with the observed changes in spirometric values therefore validating the CFD method for the studied application.

added_models.model: Tanabe-era in vitro receptor-binding kinetics of TA-2005 (carmoterol): methacholine-precontracted guinea-pig trachea relaxation with bovine trapezium beta2 binding and GppNHp shift, tight binding offered as the basis of a long duration of action

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level (paywalled); Eur J Pharmacol 227:403-409, December 1992, DOI verified on Europe PMC. pD2 9.29 vs 7.65 isoprenaline and 7.10 salbutamol; one binding state (pKd 8.2) without GppNHp. Sykes 2012 (https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1476-5381.2011.01639.x, PMC3423252, full text read) later measured carmoterol koff 0.46 min-1 (t1/2 1.5 min) in CHO-beta2 membranes with GTP and wrote that its washout duration 'is more likely to be attributable to membrane interactions and so-called drug rebinding': the mechanism was not reproduced in vitro, but that is a model-against-model test, not a patient comparison, so it changes no status.
engagement.judgement: Opening entry. A receptor-binding system, not the guinea-pig bronchoconstriction model: like the Almirall kinetics track it predicts duration from the drug-receptor interaction, so its own track. The Tanabe in vivo and organ-bath airway papers (Kikkawa 1991, Kikkawa 1994) are the same system as the Chiesi guinea-pig track and are not re-opened here.
engagement.model: Tanabe-era in vitro receptor-binding kinetics of TA-2005 (carmoterol): methacholine-precontracted guinea-pig trachea relaxation with bovine trapezium beta2 binding and GppNHp shift, tight binding offered as the basis of a long duration of action
engagement.note: Guinea-pig trachea relaxation (pD2 9.29) and bovine trapezium binding: one tight-binding state without GppNHp, offered as the basis of a long duration of action.
engagement.short: Tight binding predicted long duration for carmoterol
engagement.quote: The long duration of action of TA 2005 might be explained by tight binding of this compound to the beta 2-adrenoceptor.

engagement.magnitude_basis: tracheal relaxation pD2 9.29 and tight binding vs peak FEV1 +0.241 L over placebo at week 4; the model gave no FEV1 magnitude
engagement.confidence_note: EU Clinical Trials Register results record (EudraCT 2006-005689-38; Chiesi CSR CCD-0604-RS-0009 synopsis), the same record and quote the draft's Chiesi-track engagement entry carries (read in full by the drafter, verified by the checker; not re-downloaded here). 252 moderate-to-severe asthmatics on ICS, CHF 4226 2 ug once daily vs formoterol 12 ug twice daily vs placebo for 4 weeks; results posted 2017-01-01. Conference abstracts from 2006-2008 are not admissible.
engagement.judgement: The downstream readout moved (peak FEV1 and FEV1 AUC 0-3 h p<0.001 vs placebo), so same on engagement, as on the Chiesi track; the duration claim is scored under efficacy. Dated to the registry posting. By then Sykes 2012 had shown the tight-binding mechanism does not hold in vitro, so the bronchodilation prediction was right for a reason the model got wrong.
engagement.model: Tanabe-era in vitro receptor-binding kinetics of TA-2005 (carmoterol): methacholine-precontracted guinea-pig trachea relaxation with bovine trapezium beta2 binding and GppNHp shift, tight binding offered as the basis of a long duration of action
engagement.note: Carmoterol 2 ug once daily raised peak FEV1 0.241 L over placebo at week 4: the bronchodilation the binding assay implied; 24-h trough did not.
engagement.short: Peak FEV1 up, as tight binding implied
engagement.quote: The LS mean treatment difference between CHF 4226 and placebo for peak FEV1 after 4 weeks of treatment was 0.241 L (p <0.001 ) and for FEV1 AUC(0,3) was 0.222 L (p <0.001).

efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (paywalled). The model's only efficacy-bearing claim is duration of action; it names no airflow, symptom or exacerbation endpoint.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry: the tight-binding claim is a duration claim, which the trial primary (trough FEV1 at 24 h on once-daily dosing) tests, so the cell opens here with the model.
efficacy.model: Tanabe-era in vitro receptor-binding kinetics of TA-2005 (carmoterol): methacholine-precontracted guinea-pig trachea relaxation with bovine trapezium beta2 binding and GppNHp shift, tight binding offered as the basis of a long duration of action
efficacy.note: Binding and tracheal potency only; the model carried a duration claim but no airflow or symptom endpoint. No asthma patient readout yet.
efficacy.short: Tight binding claimed duration, no endpoint
efficacy.quote: The long duration of action of TA 2005 might be explained by tight binding of this compound to the beta 2-adrenoceptor.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: duration: tight binding offered as the basis of a long duration, against trough FEV1 +0.057 L (NS) at 24 h for 2 ug once daily vs +0.157 L for formoterol twice daily; the model gave no quantity to scale
efficacy.confidence_note: EU CTR synopsis (EudraCT 2006-005689-38; CSR CCD-0604-RS-0009 dated 2010-03-02), the same record and quote as the draft's Chiesi-track efficacy entry (read in full by the drafter, verified by the checker; not re-downloaded here); 252 randomised, results posted 2017-01-01. The 4 ug carmoterol dose later held trough FEV1 only inside the budesonide/carmoterol combination CHF 5188 (EudraCT 2008-001773-15, results posted 2017-01-01, trough +0.26 L per the checker), the 'higher dose later worked' branch left to the checker's open rule question; no monotherapy trial followed.
efficacy.judgement: Contra: the model's one claim, long duration, was tested as 2 ug once daily and trough FEV1 at 24 h did not beat placebo while formoterol twice daily did. The same trial failure sits on the Chiesi guinea-pig track; it is scored again here because this is a separate system, each track scored by its own rules.
efficacy.model: Tanabe-era in vitro receptor-binding kinetics of TA-2005 (carmoterol): methacholine-precontracted guinea-pig trachea relaxation with bovine trapezium beta2 binding and GppNHp shift, tight binding offered as the basis of a long duration of action
efficacy.note: Primary missed: carmoterol 2 ug once daily gave trough FEV1 +0.057 L (NS) at 24 h in 252 asthmatics; the tight-binding duration claim failed.
efficacy.quote: The primary efficacy analysis did not demonstrate that CHF 4226 2 µg administered once daily in the evening was statistically significant superior to placebo on trough FEV1 after 4 weeks of treatment (LS mean difference = 0.057 L).

patient_trials.quote: The primary efficacy analysis did not demonstrate that CHF 4226 2 µg administered once daily in the evening was statistically significant superior to placebo on trough FEV1 after 4 weeks of treatment (LS mean difference = 0.057 L).

considered_not_added: EU CTR 2008-001773-15 (CHF 5188 budesonide/carmoterol 400/4 ug once daily, results posted 2017-01-01): a patient-side record for the existing Chiesi guinea-pig track (efficacy 'then same', dose 'target too low'), not a new model system; also bears on the new Voss 1992 kinetics track the same way, noted in its efficacy entry.

ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00683449 (MediciNova acute-exacerbation dose-finding, results posted 2011-07-29): a patient-side record for the existing Kissei rat organ-bath track (efficacy #6 patient_trials), not a new model system.

Tanabe TA-2005 guinea-pig airway papers: Kikkawa 1991 Jpn J Pharmacol (PMID 1687479, DOI 10.1254/jjp.57.175; isolated guinea-pig trachea relaxation pD2 9.79, trachea-vs-atria selectivity, lung/ventricle binding) and Kikkawa 1994 Biol Pharm Bull (PMID 7820105, DOI 10.1248/bpb.17.1047; anaesthetised guinea-pig and cat histamine, serotonin and antigen bronchoconstriction, inhaled duration comparable or superior to salmeterol and formoterol). Same system and same prediction (potent, long-lasting guinea-pig bronchodilation) as the draft's chiesi-guinea-pig-challenge-bronchoconstriction track, so not a new track: that track's model_first_use_year should move from 2005 to 1991 (organ bath) or 1994 (in vivo). Voss 1992 is a different system (binding kinetics) and is added above.

Sykes & Charlton 2012 Br J Pharmacol CHO-beta2 competition-kinetics assay (PMID 21883146, PMC3423252, full text read): carmoterol is one of its eight agonists (koff 0.46 min-1, t1/2 1.5 min, 'almost complete dissociation ... within 5 min'), but its carmoterol comparison is with in-vitro washout duration, and its clinical onset/duration comparisons are for indacaterol, salmeterol, formoterol and salbutamol, none a member of this class. No member-drug patient comparison, so no track; recorded on the Voss 1992 track's opening note as the in-vitro contradiction of the mechanism.

Hendrickx 2018 AstraZeneca translational lung-PK model (PMID 29280349, DOI 10.1002/psp4.12270): AZD3199 is modelled, but its FEV1 comparison (Supplementary Table S5, per the COPD tile's reading) is against COPD patients (Kuna 2013), not asthma; it is the COPD tile's track and has no asthma comparison for a member.

MediciNova dog study of i.v. MN-221 with nebulised albuterol (CHEST 2010 poster, press release only): not peer-reviewed, so it cannot be model_src (tier 5 is patient-side only); no admissible model source, note-only as the checker said.

Murata 2005 BJOG 24-h pregnant-sheep infusion (PMID 15663400; the checker's 'Kanayama 2005', Kanayama is not an author on the record): the same sheep system as Kiguchi 2002, no patient comparison of its own, folded into the sheep track's opening note.

Liedtke 2019 hyperlactataemia meta-analysis (PMC7019948, tier 4): grepped, no bedoradrine, so the sheep lactate and glucose predictions have no patient record beyond House 2015's unquantified 'metabolic effects'; no status change and no entry.
ADRB2 genotype pharmacogenetics: no analysis for any member drug found (Europe PMC, 9 hits, none relevant).
Human challenge models (methacholine, allergen, exercise): no challenge study of a member drug in asthma found (22 hits, reviews only).

Patient ex-vivo systems (human isolated bronchi, airway smooth muscle cells, precision-cut lung slices, organoids): the Almirall human isolated bronchi are already inside the Almirall track; nothing else for a member.

Bjermer 2015 AZD3199 clinical pharmacokinetics (PMID 25709399): healthy-volunteer, asthma and COPD PK with no model prediction; and Bindel & Seifert 2026 database review of recombinant beta-AR affinities (PMID 42401193): not a model system.
